brief:
At a polling station in Kiryat Arba, a settlement in the southern West Bank home to far-right politician Itamar Ben Gvir, voters expressed dissatisfaction with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's approach to security, according to Al-Monitor. Resident Lishay Cooper stated the country needed a tougher leader than the famously hawkish Netanyahu.

The sentiment reflects growing pressure within Israel's far-right constituency to move beyond Netanyahu toward more hardline policies in the occupied territories.
dek: At a polling station in the Israeli settlement of Kiryat Arba, home of far-right firebrand Itamar Ben Gvir in the southern West Bank, voter Lishay Cooper said the country needed a tougher leader than famously hawkish Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
title: Israeli settlers seek far-right leader tougher than Netanyahu
